title: Twelve moves to reach square six

beats.say: Seed fourteen, trip three. One move left. Which mouse can still reach the flag?
Play the last move. Orange lands on six. Purple steps left and runs out of time.

The mice represent two learners. At each matching trip and move, they read the same random draws. Purple learned from the goal reward alone. Orange also got feedback from its distance to the goal before and after each move. Count the goals on the other trips to see how often that helped.

title: Which claim comes from the paper?

beats.say: Why would a distance bonus help? The paper gives a formula for changing the reward while preserving the best policy under its assumptions. We borrowed that formula for a seven-square corridor and a learner with a table of action values. How quickly that learner finds the goal is our experiment.

Use Keshav’s three reading passes. On the first pass, read the title, abstract and conclusion to find the question and the claimed result. On the second, check the equation, the assumptions and what the figures actually measure. Write down any detail you still need to run the comparison.

On the third pass, close the paper and reconstruct the bonus for one move. Check whether both learners get the same budget, random inputs and scoring rule. Keep the paper section beside the formula and record the corridor and seed choices in your study plan.
If a seed loses goals, mark the cause as an open question.

title: How much does one seed tell us?

beats.say: Go back to seed fourteen and count all thirty early training episodes for each learner. Purple reached the goal once. With shaping, it reached the goal twenty-one times. That's twenty extra goals on the seed we just watched.
Change only the seed. On seed six, purple reached the goal eleven times and the shaped learner reached it twice. Same corridor, same scoring rule. Which seed belongs in the study average?

Both do. Subtract sparse from shaped within each seed. Average those differences over all twenty-four planned pairs. The question is whether shaping helps this tabular learner reach the goal early and leaves its final success close to baseline. Set both rules before collecting fresh seeds. These worked rows have already been seen.

title: Construct each predicate of the research decision

beats.say: The hypothesis names an agent, environment, intervention, metric, analysis unit and rejection rule. Here each independently generated simulator seed supplies a pair of first-thirty-episode success fractions. Subtract sparse from shaped within each seed, then average all planned differences.

The declared early rule requires a mean at least plus point one zero and a ninety-percent interval whose lower bound is strictly above zero. The final guardrail separately requires its observed mean and entire ninety-percent paired interval within minus point zero two through plus point zero two.

Try a mean gain of nine points, with a lower limit of two. The interval clears zero. Does the early result pass? Nine still falls short of ten. Now try a mean of thirteen with a lower limit of four. Early learning passes. If the final interval extends three points below zero, the combined claim fails.
To claim a gain of more than ten percentage points at ninety-percent confidence, the lower end of the early interval must be above ten. Here it reaches down to four.

title: Keep known worked output outside a fresh confirmatory plan

beats.say: The article's twenty-four worked seeds have already been observed. Rerun them to check repeatability. For a new confirmation, debug on pilot seeds, then freeze the hypothesis, variables, decision and exclusion rules. Reserve untouched seeds. Suppose we saw seeds eighty and eighty-one before locking a plan for eighty through eighty-three. Completing all four would still leave two observed pilots in the sample.

A retained commit identifies a plan version, while a timestamped read-only registration preserves the before-data commitment. Record amendments and their timing. If a terminal bug is discovered after several observed seeds, retain the invalid outputs, version the correction and rerun the complete corrected comparison rather than mixing old and new implementations.

Because the observed outcomes influenced development, label that corrected run amended evidence. A new untouched sample is needed for a fresh confirmatory claim. Run all planned pairs under the registered failure and rerun policy; an unfavorable result is not a mechanical failure or a valid exclusion by itself.

title: Keep the simulator’s authority as small as its claim

beats.say: The local study generates its own transitions from configuration and pseudorandom inputs. It uses CPU and NumPy, with left and right as simulator actions. It does not need customer messages, production logs, external model APIs or live account actions.

A public-safe submission still needs review for credentials, machine paths, usernames and third-party license restrictions. Release only code and assets you have authority to share. Synthetic inputs make this particular data boundary simple; they do not turn a simulator result into evidence about user behavior, robotics or deployed-agent safety.

title: Reconstruct the actual transition contract

beats.say: Every episode begins at state zero in a corridor from zero through six. Action zero intends left and action one intends right. A slip below probability point one five reverses the intended movement, then the environment clamps the new position to the endpoints.

The original environment reward is one on reaching state six, otherwise zero. Goal arrival terminates the episode. The collection loop also stops after twelve steps without success. Retain starting state, intended action, realized successor, original reward and ending reason as separate diagnostic facts.

The actual learner uses discount point nine five, step size point three five and epsilon point two for eighty training episodes. The early metric covers only the first thirty. A complete capstone retains transition traces too; the compact script preserves successes and step counts, which cannot identify the causal transition behind a particular seed regression.

title: Turn a potential into a training signal

beats.say: A sparse reward appears only when the learner reaches the goal. Define a potential that increases as the agent approaches it. The candidate adds discounted next potential minus current potential to its training reward, supplying feedback before the first successful journey.

Try the first step right. With discount point nine five, discount the successor potential, minus five sixths, then subtract the starting potential, minus one. The bonus is about plus point two zero eight. Reverse that step and the bonus is minus point one one seven. Now push left against the starting wall. Both potentials are minus one. The bonus is still plus point zero five, and the goal counter stays at zero. In final evaluation both learners receive only the original goal reward.

title: Cancel the interior potential terms across a whole path

beats.say: The potential is negative distance to the goal divided by six. For each transition, add discount times next potential minus current potential to the training reward. Discount each transition’s addition again by its time index when summing the return.

Adjacent interior potentials cancel: the positive discounted next potential from one step meets the negative current potential from the next. The remaining total is negative initial potential plus discount to the path length multiplied by final potential.
Both a direct completed path and a longer detour from state zero end at zero potential, giving the same total addition, plus one.

A stationary step can earn a local bonus. In an infinite discounted task with bounded potential, the last term vanishes in the limit. At a finite collection cap it can survive. Try a three-step example with discount point eight and starting potential minus point seven five. At a zero-potential goal the addition is point seven five. Stop instead at potential minus point two five. The boundary term subtracts point one two eight, leaving point six two two.

title: Distinguish an observation cap from a terminal task state

beats.say: The underlying learning task here has no twelve-step deadline. The timeout is an external collection cap, so the last non-goal state still has estimated future value. The Q target therefore includes discounted best next-state value at a timeout, but not at the true terminal goal.

The reported success metric nevertheless asks whether the goal was reached within twelve collected steps. That measurement and the underlying discounted-learning objective are related but different. If a deadline were part of the task, include remaining time in the state and treat expiry as terminal.

Keep terminal and truncation flags distinct in the implementation and tests. Bootstrapping through a true goal or dropping the next-state term merely because collection stopped changes the target. Writing the correct shaping formula does not repair a wrong task-ending contract.

title: Update the state and intended action that produced the transition

beats.say: A Q-table stores estimated future reward for each state and action. An action can slip and move the agent in the opposite direction. Record the starting state, intended action and realized successor separately. The update belongs to the starting state and intended action, even when physical movement went left instead.

In this practice update, use step size point two and an old entry of zero. A right choice slips from one to zero. The bonus is negative. With a next value of zero, the entry falls. Supply a next value of point four instead. The discounted future value outweighs the bonus and the same entry rises. At a true goal, drop the future value. At a collection timeout, keep it for this underlying task.

title: Compute the study’s complete intended-action update

beats.say: For the actual study update, compute target minus old Q, multiply by step size point three five and add it to the old entry. At starting state one, an intended right action that slips to zero updates Q of one and right. It does not update the successor state’s right entry.

With zero initial values and no goal reward, the shaping term is approximately minus point one one six seven. The target is that term and the updated entry becomes approximately minus point zero four zero eight three.
Now keep the same transition but supply a next-state maximum point four. The target becomes about point two six three three, so a zero old entry would rise to point zero nine two one seven.

The earlier constructed picture uses step size point two to isolate that same sign change. The executed article study uses point three five. Keep those illustrative and study parameters identified. A negative immediate bonus alone does not determine the complete target or update direction. To use a nonzero old value, subtract it from the target first. Multiply that difference by the step size, then add the old value back.

title: Which draw starts the next trip?

beats.say: Imagine two readers on identical slip tapes. To see the indexing problem, suppose purple uses six draws on trip one and orange uses twelve. Where would their readers stop on a continuous tape? Purple points to draw seven. Orange points to thirteen.

Go back to the last draw each mouse used. Give each trip its own row of twelve draws. Each of the four tapes has eighty rows. They supply an exploration check, a random action, a tie-break and a slip draw. Start trip two. Advance both readers to the first cell of row two. Six unused cells stay behind on purple's first row.

Now follow the seed-zero slip tape to the fourth move of trip two. The draw is about point zero six, below the slip threshold of point one five. Try two different choices. That draw reverses a left choice to right and a right choice to left. Both learners read the same cell.
Each still chooses its own action from its learned values or its exploration draw.

title: Where did the zero-potential update land?

beats.say: Set the potential to zero. The candidate should now give exactly the same updates as sparse training. Try a small fault. Let the candidate write to the direction it traveled. Start at square one and choose right.
Both neighboring squares have a best next value of point four. On an ordinary right move both tables put point one three three under right. The equality check passes.
Reset the tables and let that same right action slip left. Keep the reward, step size and next value fixed. Which entry should receive the update?

Sparse credits the right action that was chosen. Our faulty candidate credits left. The numbers have the same size and the arrays differ. Stop here. An implementation fault can change learning even when the bonus is zero.

Write to the intended action in both tables. Now the entries match on the slip too. The full study checks the whole Q table, the episode successes and the step counts on every seed. Once those match, compare the distance bonus.
Freeze the trained tables and score both on separate shared evaluation draws using the original goal reward.

title: Compute what pairing changes in estimator variance

beats.say: For independent, identically distributed seed pairs, the variance of the mean difference is the sum of the two arm variances minus twice their covariance, all divided by the number of pairs. Independently sampled arms omit that covariance term. With the same marginal variances and sample sizes, positive covariance lowers paired variance, zero changes nothing, and negative covariance raises it.

The article’s five invented baseline scores run from zero through one in quarter steps, with candidate equal to one minus baseline. Their sample covariance is minus point one five six two five. Both marginal variances are point one five six two five.

Divide the two variances' sum by five for an independent estimate of point zero six two five. Subtract twice the negative covariance first, then divide by five, and the paired variance doubles to point one two five.

Read the leftmost pair. The candidate gains a full point. At the rightmost pair it loses a full point. Across all five pairs, what do the gains and losses average? The mean difference is zero, even though pairing doubled the estimated variance of that mean here. When the study pairs runs by seed, resample each seed’s two scores together. Use their observed covariance to judge precision.

title: Freeze learned tables before the separate evaluation tape

beats.say: Pilot seeds nine hundred through nine hundred two are for debugging and stay outside the worked primary sample. New confirmatory seeds must also stay untouched until their plan is frozen. A seed number alone does not define a complete random stream without its generator, call sequence and environment.

For final evaluation, freeze each learned Q table. The evaluator uses a separate slip tape seeded with ten thousand plus the training seed, shared by the two policies. It chooses greedy actions and records two hundred episode successes under original goal reward, without training updates or a shaping bonus.

If you use these scores to pick the bonus, they become tuning data. Evaluate that choice on fresh seeds. To test whether shaping helps in another environment, repeat the comparison there. To repeat this corridor test on another machine, keep the generator, its sequence of calls and the software environment with the seeds.

title: Change one identified component per comparison

beats.say: The zero-potential row checks whether candidate code reduces exactly to sparse training. The distance-potential row changes only the training reward for the primary comparison. Both require the same environment and measurement contract.

The independent-arm sensitivity row resamples already completed outcomes using separate indices. It is not another training run or a new sample. The reversed-potential row changes the potential sign as an exploratory stress test; it cannot redefine a result already observed.

Preserve all row configurations and their decision roles. An ablation changes a named factor to investigate its mechanism. Choosing the best row of an unplanned hyperparameter search and calling it the primary ablation makes selection depend on the result.

title: Retain mechanical attempts before deriving the primary table

beats.say: Plan the run table before execution. Name the seed set, training and evaluation budgets, output and decision role. Watch one illustrative attempt move from planned to running. If the output cannot be written, record a mechanical failure. A completed run with a low score belongs in the results. Exclude a run only under a locked rule.

A permitted rerun retains the original failed attempt, error and linked replacement. Sort results by seed, not performance. Point the aggregate summary to the complete row-table reference so an outsider can reconstruct it rather than rely on a screenshot or a favorable subset.

title: Keep the negative seeds in the picture

beats.say: Read one column per seed. Its height is the change in goals in the first thirty trips. Orange beats purple above zero. Below zero, the shaped learner loses goals. Count the columns below the line. Five pairs favor the sparse reward. They are seeds six, eleven, seventeen, nineteen and twenty-three. The mean across all twenty-four is still positive.

Removing the negative points would improve the headline by selecting on the outcome. Keep them and investigate explanations with diagnostic traces or a new study. The table alone cannot establish which particular slip or exploration decision caused a seed’s regression.

title: What goes back into the draw?

beats.say: Take four of our seed rows for practice. Each fraction tells you how many extra goals shaping produced in thirty early episodes. Draw a row, copy it, and leave the original on the table. Take seed six twice, then seed fourteen, then seed zero.
What average gain did that draw produce? Count both copies of six.

The four differences add up to five extra goals. Divide by four times thirty. Multiply the resulting fraction by a hundred. That's about four point two percentage points. This is one possible resampled mean from our four-row example.

In the study each draw takes twenty-four whole pairs from the full table. Episodes within a run share a learner that keeps updating, so individual episodes can't serve as independent repeats of the experiment.

title: Where do the interval endpoints come from?

beats.say: Put all twenty-four retained seed pairs back on the table and draw twenty-four times with replacement. Average those selected differences to get one mean. Repeat that draw ten thousand times with the study's fixed bootstrap seed.

Sort the ten thousand means from smallest to largest. For a percentile, multiply its probability by the number of gaps between the means. That gives a position between two neighbors. Use the fractional part to interpolate. The fifth and ninety-fifth percentiles give a ninety-percent interval from six point one to twenty-two point five percentage points.
For a pair of different neighbors, take two sorted means of four and twelve percentage points. Suppose the rank falls one quarter of the way between them. What value belongs there?

A quarter of that eight-point gap is two. Add two to four and you get six points. Back in the actual run, the two neighbors for each endpoint have the same value, so interpolation leaves each endpoint where it is.

Keep the generator, seed and resampling method with these numbers. A different draw or a bias-corrected interval can move the endpoints. Each draw can only select pairs we observed. A rare outcome missing from those seeds stays missing, and the interval describes variation under this procedure. Treat the seed pairs as independent draws under a fixed procedure. Ninety percent describes the intended coverage across repeated samples. Choosing a rule after seeing the data adds uncertainty this interval does not capture.

title: Where does the lower endpoint fall?

beats.say: The gold dot is the average gain over all twenty-four seeds, fourteen point three percentage points. The dot clears ten and the lower endpoint clears zero, so the early rule passes.

Now suppose the report says the gain is at least ten points at ninety-percent confidence. Look at the left tip. It reaches down to six point one points, below ten. That interval allows a smaller gain than the headline promises.

All nineteen gains and five regressions contributed to this interval. Keeping only the gains would raise the mean to nearly twenty-four points. Resampling the arms separately made the interval about fifteen percent wider for these rows. With a different pattern of paired scores, the change in width can go the other way.

title: How many goals are behind a tie?

beats.say: Now freeze the learned tables and play two hundred evaluation episodes on the original goal reward. On seed eighteen, the difference between the two success rates is zero. Could both learners have missed the goal more than half the time?

Open the scores. Each learner reached the goal ninety-one times in two hundred episodes. Both fell short of the halfway mark. Across the whole study, every final pair tied, so the paired bootstrap interval for the observed differences collapses to zero. That checks the declared final guardrail in this sample.
To explain this particular pair's low score, look at the move its frozen policy makes at the start.

title: Explain the weak absolute policy from its actual action table

beats.say: Inspect seed eighteen’s actual learned greedy actions. Both policies choose left at state zero and right at states one through five. An intended left at the left boundary stays at zero unless a slip reverses it, so leaving the start depends on that reversal.

On seed eighteen, each learner reached the flag on ninety-one of two hundred trips. Each missed it a hundred and nine times. That pair contributes a zero to the final comparison. Under the theorem’s assumptions, potential-based shaping preserves which policies are optimal. The tie leaves open whether either learner found one in eighty training trips.

title: Keep episode count, transitions and time as separate budgets

beats.say: Both arms train for eighty episodes, but early goal arrival can shorten an episode. The retained rows average seven hundred seventy-three point two five transitions for sparse training and seven hundred fifty-four point seven for shaped training. Episode count therefore does not imply equal environment-step work.

This design measures early success per episode. A same-step-budget study or wall-clock efficiency claim needs its own controlled budget and measured time. Record training transitions, evaluation work and actual duration separately; do not convert fewer steps into an unmeasured hardware speedup.

title: Reconstruct the data from its actual origin

beats.say: To reconstruct synthetic data, retain the generator version and source, seed range, state count, transition and slip rule, step cap and exact command. Mark the rows you keep as references and the files you can regenerate. In a separate checkout, open the article’s illustrations directory. The command on screen runs that copy of the exporter.

For a later public-dataset extension, retain its original location, license, version, retrieval date, checksum, preprocessing command and excluded rows. If a filter removes row one hundred eight, keep its identifier and the reason beside the preprocessing command. A renamed local file does not replace that origin. Compare the retained inputs, source and configuration before treating a new output as a repeat of the same experiment.

title: Bind source, environment and outputs without inventing authority

beats.say: A commit identifies a tracked tree, excluding dirty and untracked files. Retain the executed source snapshot too, with documented file ordering and encoding. Compare its digest with an independently retained expected snapshot; a self-reported hash does not exclude an edit.

Record the interpreter, actual package and build versions, lockfile, operating system, architecture and relevant numerical libraries. A Python patch-version range or a dependency lock does not pin every host property. NumPy’s detailed stream-compatibility conditions include generator, seed, method calls, arguments, build and environment.

Preserve configuration bytes and their history, then hash seed rows and derived outputs against a retained original. A new hash cannot establish when a file changed. Output identity, actual execution, scientific validity and producer identity require different evidence; an unsigned consistent manifest cannot authenticate who performed the run.

title: Compare byte identity before claiming a successful rerun

beats.say: Compare two files that encode the same seed and success rate. One fits on a line and one has indentation. Their decoded values agree. Their byte digests differ. For a numerical rerun, lock the fields and tolerance first. With a tolerance of ten millionths, a difference of nine millionths passes. Keep both byte digests and both files.

I can type a perfect score and compute the file’s checksum. You can match that checksum without running the study. Run the saved code with the same inputs. Does your success rate match mine within the tolerance we set in advance? If it falls outside that tolerance, keep both outputs and investigate before editing the report.

title: Derive the figure and report from the executed row source

beats.say: The included exporter reads the uniquely named experiment code fence, executes it, and writes the seed CSV, result JSON and a manifest. The figure reads that result JSON rather than a second manually typed result list. Source, exporter, configuration and output digests help compare the resulting files.

Both checkouts contain the seed table. Keep the reference read-only. Look at the command in the separate checkout. Which table will it write? Run that checkout’s copy of the exporter from the article’s illustrations directory. It writes the CSV, result JSON and manifest beside that script. Compare those files with the retained originals under the declared rule. A full environment lock and evidence of who ran the study take separate records.

A complete submission adds the documented command and lock, plan history, diagnostic traces, license and citation metadata. A root citation file supplies machine-readable software authorship and release information; an archived persistent identifier helps find the exact release. These are proposed package requirements beyond the miniature’s exported three files.

title: What do you do with a failed check?

beats.say: Suppose the zero-potential control differs from sparse training. Trace the first update where the tables disagree. If a clean clone stops on a missing dependency, fix the package and rerun the command. Record the failed attempt alongside the repair.

If the early interval crosses zero, the direction of the gain is uncertain under the study rule. If the mean falls below ten points, it misses the practical target. If the final interval leaves the two-point band, the combined claim fails.
Report that decision with the same seed rows and deviations you would show for a passing run.

Look at seed six. With shaping, the learner reached the goal twice in thirty trips. With sparse rewards, it got there eleven times. Where did the extra misses come from? A trace records the intended move, the slip draw and the square where the learner landed.
Keep seed six in the table. To test whether early slips account for the losses, plan that comparison on fresh runs.

title: Would the gain carry over to a branching grid?

beats.say: The worked corridor gives the learner two directions on one line. Open a side passage at square three. At the junction the learner now has another choice. Which route will the shaped learner take? We have no observations beyond this junction. Run the same reward comparison on the branching grid and measure the change in early goals and final success.

To test a neural learner, replace the table with a network. To test the reward formula, choose the potential functions in advance. Try each learning-rate setting on the same planned seeds, and choose the number of seeds for the precision you need.

A study about an agent in use needs measurements from its intended task, including any safety outcomes you want to claim. Report the corridor result with its learner, training budget and seed procedure. Name the change you would test next and what you would measure.

title: Exercise the evidence before advancing its status

beats.say: At the first milestone, another engineer traces the equation and assumptions to source and predicts what would support or reject the locked claim. Submit the triage, plan, public boundary and expected result before confirmatory outputs exist.

At the second, exercise the simulator and sparse baseline on pilot data, inspect a transition and verify exact zero-potential equality. Include config schema, dependency lock and one clean command before running the new confirmatory sample.

At the third, retain every planned seed row, actual resampling output, deviations, manifests and derived figures. A reviewer recomputes headline values and reruns a seed pair. At the fourth, they start from a clean clone, produce the primary table and identify an unsupported inference beside the final report, license and talk.

Feedback that changes the locked design creates an amendment before the next confirmatory run. A file called a manifest or a folder called reviews is not the evidence by itself. The reviewer must actually exercise the stated layer and record its result.

title: Use the claim and its evidence to allocate the presentation

beats.say: The proposed ten-minute talk spends eight minutes on seven evidence jobs: problem, source claim, hypothesis, design, result, failure checks and limitations. The supplied segments total four hundred eighty seconds, leaving one hundred twenty for questions. Practice that actual allocation instead of taking the audience through a directory tree.

Prepare answers with artifact links. Why this seed budget? Show precision and variation. Why can five seeds regress? Separate the mean from individual outcomes. Did shaping change the task? Show original-reward evaluation and theorem assumptions. Why do equal final scores not establish skill? Show the absolute per-seed rates.

Keep table, figure and report derived from the same retained rows. A caption should interpret the five regressions and interval, not repeat its title. Use sign, position and labels alongside color. Disclose deviations, and do not improvise a causal explanation that the diagnostic evidence never established.

title: Name the actual independent evidence layer

beats.say: Who ran the code, and whose code was it? If the authors recover their result on the same setup, ACM calls that repeatability. In this example, team B used the authors’ files and got a match within the declared tolerance. Label that run reproducibility. Team C wrote its own implementation from the paper. Their result matched too. Which label fits when the team and the code both change? Label that run replicability.

Hand the package to a reviewer. Can they follow the instructions, find every file the paper calls for, and run the study? Have them verify the output. From all twenty-four pairs, can they recover the reported gain of fourteen point three percentage points? Record what they exercised. A download shows availability. Reuse and independent validation each need their own evidence. Record a badge only when the review awards it.

FAIR adds findability, accessibility, interoperability and reuse. Accessible data may require authentication and authorization; it need not be unrestricted. Persistent identifiers, open formats, provenance and a license support reuse while leaving the need for actual executable validation intact.

title: Would you sign off on this figure?

beats.say: A colleague sends you a draft figure. It claims a gain of almost twenty-four percentage points. You have the study plan and the original seed table. Before you sign off, count the rows behind the figure. Nineteen pairs made it into the calculation. The plan calls for twenty-four. Which rows would you look for?

Start with seed six. Its nine lost goals belong in the sum. Put back the other four regressions too. Together the five rows subtract thirty-three goals and add a hundred fifty early episodes per arm. The learners haven't changed. What gain should the rebuilt figure report?

A hundred three net goals across seven hundred twenty early episodes per arm gives fourteen point three percentage points. Rebuild the figure and its paired interval from all twenty-four rows. Hand over the plan, executed source, config, environment and clean rerun command with that table.
Keep the reference outputs so the next researcher can compare the rerun. A checksum compares bytes. A recorded rerun shows whether the experiment repeats.

title: Which claims would you keep?

beats.say: Try a new report with supplied measurements. On the early ruler the mean is thirteen points and its ninety-percent interval runs from four to twenty-two. On the magnified final ruler the mean and its ninety-percent interval sit inside the two-point band.

The two final success rates are forty-two percent and forty-two and a half percent. Keep the study's original rules. The draft claims a gain of at least ten points at ninety-percent confidence and calls the final policies competent. Which claims can you defend from these measurements?

The early rule passes because the mean clears ten points and the lower end clears zero. The final rule passes because the mean and the whole interval fit inside the band. Four points is still compatible with the early data, and both policies reached the goal in fewer than half their evaluation episodes.

Keep every measured value and edit the draft. Report that the mean gain passed the early rule and final success stayed similar under the declared guardrail. Give the interval and both absolute rates so a reader can see how small the gain could be and how often the policies missed.
Keep the mean differences and both final scores. Change just one endpoint. Move the lower final limit to minus three points. The upper end stays put. Can the report still say both rules pass?

Withhold support for the combined claim. The lower end extends past minus two even though the final mean sits inside the band. Keep the early finding and report the failed guardrail beside it. In the next lesson you'll compare ways to train sentence embeddings.
Before you call one better, decide which evidence could change your mind.
